1: Nominal seasonal catch per tow-hour for herring, sablefish, Chinook salmon, chum salmon, and pollock in EBS pollock-dominated hauls, 1991–2026. Rates equal total extrapolated catch divided by total valid tow-hours. Units are kg per tow-hour for herring and sablefish, tons per tow-hour for pollock, and fish per tow-hour for salmon. A season is January–May; B season is June–December. Hauls are in NMFS areas 500–539, with positive total catch and more than 80% pollock by weight. The 2026 B-season data extend through September 18. Missing species catches are omitted from catch sums while their tow-hours remain in the denominator; unreported species-season combinations appear as gaps. Catcher-vessel and electronic-monitoring coverage is incomplete; catcher-vessel records are absent in 2025–2026 after filtering.
2: Estimated EBS pollock catch numbers (thousands of fish) by sex for the A season (January–May), B season (June–December), and annual total, 1991–2025. Circles denote females and triangles denote males. B-season estimates combine northwest and southeast areas; annual totals equal A + B. Shading marks provisional 2024–2025 estimates based on released FT-NIRS ages before conversion to thin-section tester ages. Both years cover all 12 months. The estimates have limited age–length coverage: approximately 0.50% and 0.36% of catch biomass, respectively, remain unallocated in unsupported cells.
4: Pollock roe production for the A (January–May) and B (June–December) seasons, 2000–2026. Data combine at-sea Bering Sea and inshore Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands (BSAI) production. Values are roe product metric tons. Open markers and dashed links identify provisional 2026 values through October 2026.
10: Weekly B-season (defined here as weeks 25–40) distributions of mean pollock weight, 2001–2026. Catch tons are grouped in approximately 66.7-g bins; the vertical line marks 500 g. The 2026 series extends through September 18 and covers only part of this window. Available catcher-vessel coverage is incomplete.
12: EBS bottom-trawl survey (BTS) pollock CPUE and bottom-temperature contours, 2018–2026 (no survey was conducted in 2020), reproduced from the AKsf R-package’s pollock-mapping example (Ianelli 2026). Blue points mark sampled tows; contours are labeled 0, 2 and 4 °C. Surfaces are descriptive local interpolations within survey coverage, with no spatial prediction intervals. The CPUE includes a density-dependent correction whose version and adoption status are unspecified in the example.
21: Annual AVO relative backscatter index for 2009–2026, with the 95% confidence intervals rescaled by the same mean. The dashed line marks a relative index of 1. The line has a gap at 2020; the orange triangle identifies 2026.
23: Observed and predicted weight-at-age, 2014–2028, after omitting 2026 BTS weight observations from the standalone random-effects fit. Cell labels give mean weight in kg per fish for ages 3–10. Fishery and BTS observations end in 2025; the right-hand panel includes 2026 estimates without weight observations and 2027–2028 forecasts. The solid line marks 2026; dashed boxes mark forecast years. Colours show proportional deviations from each age’s mean through 2025 within its own panel, saturating at ±50%. Blank cells indicate absent observations, including the 2020 BTS gap.
24: Cumulative input-update comparisons within Model 23.0, 2000–2026. Each fit includes the preceding updates. Biomass uses the same population-weight schedule in every comparison, and fishing mortality is the maximum realized rate across ages. ATS and AVO updates combine observations, historical revisions and observation-error calibrations. Lines show point estimates.
25: Projected 2027 spawning biomass and combined abundance at ages 1–3 across five selected cumulative Model 23.0 input-update stages. These comparisons use estimated annual 2026 catch of 1,310,000 t. The displayed stages are cumulative; the omitted weight-at-age and A-season spawning-weight updates remain included in the fishery-age and later stages. Lower-panel columns stack ages 1, 2 and 3 at the start of 2027, before removals; spawning biomass includes mortality to spawning time. Projection methods are described in the technical supplement.
26: Approximate distributions of spawning-biomass change from 2026 to 2027 across five selected cumulative input-update stages, followed by Models 23.2 and 26.0 fitted to the same assessment data. These comparisons use estimated annual 2026 catch of 1,310,000 t. The displayed stages are cumulative; the omitted weight-at-age and A-season spawning-weight updates remain included in the fishery-age and later stages. Green area represents an increase and orange area a decrease. Dots show estimated changes, bars show 95% local asymptotic ranges, and labels give approximate chances of an increase rounded to whole percentages. Distributions use fitted parameter covariance; projection methods are described in the technical supplement.
27: Approximate distributions of change from 2025 to 2026 in total numbers at ages 1–4. Five selected cumulative input-update stages are followed by Models 23.2 and 26.0 fitted to the same assessment data. The displayed stages are cumulative; the omitted weight-at-age and A-season spawning-weight updates remain included in the fishery-age and later stages. Annual totals sum ages 1–4 at the start of the year and account for cross-age and cross-year parameter covariance. Green area represents an increase and orange area a decrease. Dots show estimates, bars show 95% uncertainty ranges and labels give approximate chances of an increase.
31: Model 26.0 start-of-year numbers at age, 1964–2026, displayed across two pages. Cells show abundance relative to each age group’s 1964–2026 mean, rounded to one decimal place, with asymptotic CV (%) in parentheses. Ages 10–14 and 15+ are pooled into 10+; its SE accounts for the full fitted parameter covariance. Both pages use the same scales and cell sizes.
32: Age-1 recruitment from the accepted 2024 assessment, Model 23.0, compared with Models 26.0 (panel A) and 26.1.2 (panel B). Bars show point estimates for both sexes in billions of fish. Historical estimates are shown without intervals. Whiskers show local 95% log-scale intervals: the native asymptotic covariance for Model 26.0 and the marginal fit’s Louis observed information for Model 26.1.2, conditional on its integration samples and normalizer grid. Calendar year denotes age 1; the 2018 year class enters at age 1 in 2019.
34: Model 26.0 log recruits per spawner. Age-1 recruits in year t+1 (million fish) are divided by female spawning biomass in year t (thousand tons), then natural-log transformed. The numerical ratio is recruits per kilogram of female spawning biomass. Upper panel: birth-year series, 1964–2025. Lower panel: the same ratios against spawning biomass, with two-digit birth-year labels and lines joining consecutive years. Orange identifies the less certain 2023–2025 year classes. The figure shows point estimates of the ratio.
36: Model 26.0 instantaneous fishing mortality by age through 2026. Tiles and contours show the same realized total fishing mortality rates; 15+ is the terminal age group.
37: Model 26.0 spawning exploitation for spawning-to-spawning intervals starting in 1964–2026. Black lines show the Model 26.0 fit; dashed blue lines and shading show MCMC posterior medians and central 95% credible intervals from 5,000 draws. Each within-draw ratio compares next-spawning biomass with and without fishing from a shared spawning-date population. The terminal interval assumes 1.375 million t catch in 2027, within-draw mean 1978–2023 recruitment and mean 2023–2025 selectivity, and the deterministic fishery-weight schedule. Biology is fixed. The terminal posterior median is 14.5333%, with interval 11.2075–18.3700%.
38: Observed indices and Model 26.0 fitted predictions. Black points show observations, lines show fitted predictions, and bars show approximate 95% observation-error ranges. BTS observation errors include covariance among survey years. The ATS age-1 panel uses a logarithmic scale in billions of fish; the 2020 age-1 placeholder is distinguished from the real 2020 USV biomass observation.
39: Model 26.0 index residuals relative to the selected observation errors, with BTS accounting for covariance among survey years. Dashed lines mark the standard-normal 95% reference range. The 2020 ATS age-1 placeholder is distinguished and excluded from observed-index summaries; the 2020 USV biomass remains an observation.
40: Annual fishery selectivity at ages 1–15+ from Model 26.0. Each ridge shows the estimated age pattern for that year.
41: Annual bottom-trawl survey selectivity at ages 1–15+ from Model 26.0. Each ridge is divided by its maximum over the displayed ages. Model curves are also shown for years without age-composition samples.
42: Annual acoustic-trawl survey selectivity at ages 2–15+ from Model 26.0. ATS and AVO share the estimated curve; age 1 is excluded. Curves are also shown for years without age-composition samples.
43: Observed grouped mean age for ATS, BTS and fishery with Model 26.0 predictions and the Model 26.1.2 fishery prediction. Bars are the observed mean ±2 SE, where SE = sqrt(sum[p_obs × (age score − observed mean)^2] / N), using the selected observed proportions and likelihood input N. Ages 1–14 and 15+ are scored 1–15; ATS excludes structural age 1 and the retained 2020 substitute. The alternative prediction is evaluated at its fitted conditional selectivity-state modes. Bars show uncertainty in the observations.
44: Fishery observed age proportions (cohort-colored bars) and Model 26.0 fitted proportions (points joined by lines), 1964–2008. Annual panels are arranged down columns and then across, with a common proportion scale. Each panel shows its year and likelihood sample size N. Age 15+ combines older cohorts.
45: Fishery observed age proportions (cohort-colored bars) and Model 26.0 fitted proportions (points joined by lines), 2009–2025. The proportion scale and cohort colors match the earlier-year figure. Each panel shows its year and likelihood sample size N; age 15+ combines older cohorts.
46: Bottom-trawl survey observed age proportions and Model 26.0 fitted proportions, 1982–2026. Annual panels share a proportion scale; the 2020 panel marks the absence of a survey. Labels give likelihood sample sizes. Age 15+ combines older cohorts.
47: Acoustic-trawl survey observed and Model 26.0 fitted age proportions, 1994–2026. Empty panels mark years without age-composition observations. The 2020 placeholder composition is excluded. Panels show observed proportions, fitted proportions and likelihood sample sizes on a common scale.
48: Standard afscOSA v0.0.1 diagnostics for Model 26.0, with fishery, BTS and ATS columns. Rows show aggregate observed and fitted compositions with 95% conditional observation ranges, normal-reference QQ plots with SDNR and tail summaries, OSA residual bubbles, and Pearson residual bubbles. ATS age 1 and the 2020 placeholder composition are excluded. Aggregate ranges condition on the fit; parameter and posterior predictive uncertainty are outside their scope.
50: ATS-q negative log marginal density and likelihood profile for Model 26.0. Panel A compares the negative log of the MCMC marginal density, normalized to integrate to one, with the optimized profile NLL. Each curve is measured relative to its own minimum over ATS q. The marginal density uses a kernel estimate from all 5,000 saved draws. Panel B pairs weighted quadratic regressions fitted directly to all 5,000 MCMC component values with profile NLL contributions for composition data, index data and selectivity deviates. The smoothers use individual draws and are displayed over the central 99% of sampled ATS q. MCMC curves are centered at the ATS-q marginal mode; profile components retain the profile minimum as their reference. These smoothers describe conditional mean native objective components; the negative log marginal density has no unique additive decomposition into those components. Other is omitted.
51: MCMC pairs plot of ATS catchability, 2026 abundance at ages 2–5, age-1 abundance in 2019 (the 2018 year class), and projected 2027 female spawning biomass for Model 26.0. Lower-triangle panels show paired values from 5,000 MCMC draws; upper-triangle panels give posterior Pearson correlations. Diagonal panels show marginal densities. Abundances are in billion fish and female SSB in million tons. The 2027 projection uses 1,375 kt catch, mean 2023–2025 fishery selectivity and within-draw mean 1978–2023 recruitment, with biological schedules fixed.
52: Retrospective trajectories for Model 26.0 (left) and Model 26.1.2 with fixed process SDs (right). Black lines show each analysis’s matched full 2026 reference; colors identify the nine peels ending in 2017–2025, and symbols mark their endpoints. Female spawning biomass is in million tons, age-1 recruitment is in billion fish, and maximum fishing mortality across ages is per year. Recruitment is indexed by the calendar year fish enter age 1. Panels show point estimates.
53: Historical retrospectives of beginning-of-year age-3+ EBS pollock biomass. Gray lines show archived 2007–2023 assessments; orange shows the official 2024 SAFE Table 27 estimates through 2024; blue shows Model 26.0 estimates through 2026. Biomass sums beginning-of-year numbers at ages 3–15+ multiplied by the corresponding annual fishery weights at age, using the Model 26.0 fit. Historical series use assessment-specific biomass definitions and may include next-year estimates. The 2024 tabulated values are rounded. No new assessment fit was produced in 2025. These are point estimates from successive assessments, encompassing changes in data, methods and biological inputs.
54: Annual age-composition sample sizes used in Model 26.0 and their Francis diagnostic equivalents for the fishery, BTS and ATS. The comparison evaluates weighting; the assessment input weights are unchanged.
55: Standardized mean-age residuals used in the Francis diagnostic comparison for Model 26.0, with the selected input sample sizes. Positive values indicate older observed than predicted mean age.
56: Annual fishery selectivity from Models 26.0 and 26.1.0. The split configuration separates Foreign and Modern domestic fisheries.
57: Fishery selectivity before and after the fleet split, with signed 1991-minus-1990 differences by age for Models 26.0 and 26.1.0.
58: Model 26.0 fishery age-composition fits, displayed separately for the Foreign (1964–1990, left) and Modern domestic (1991–2025, right) periods for comparison with Model 26.1.2. Model 26.0 fits one fishery. Row A compares sample-weighted observed age proportions (bars) with fitted proportions (black lines). Row B compares observed annual mean ages and approximate 95% sampling intervals with fitted mean ages. Row C shows observed minus fitted proportions in percentage points: open red circles indicate observations above the fit, and filled blue circles indicate observations below it. Bubble area shows the difference magnitude on the same scale as the Model 26.1.2 figure. Mean ages treat 15+ as age 15.
59: Model 26.1.2 fishery age-composition fits from the conditional fit with fixed process SDs. Columns show the Foreign and Modern domestic fisheries. Row A compares sample-weighted observed and fitted age proportions; row B compares observed annual mean ages and approximate 95% sampling intervals with fitted mean ages; row C shows observed minus fitted proportions in percentage points. Observations, likelihood weights, age ranges and bubble scale match the Model 26.0 figure. Mean-age intervals describe observation sampling uncertainty; fitted curves are point estimates. Mean ages treat 15+ as age 15.
61: Native SparseNUTS pairs diagnostic for the six parameters with the lowest bulk effective sample size in the newly fitted regularized Model 26.0 posterior. Lower panels show all 5,000 retained draws in black, the saved regularized native MAP as a red dot, and the 95% bivariate Normal approximation from the matching full inverse augmented Hessian as a red ellipse. Upper panels report pooled posterior Pearson correlations. Diagonal panels show four retained chain traces, bulk ESS and R-hat. Parameters retain their native coordinate scales. Local ranges are calculated at the regularized MAP, distinct from the production penalized-ML fit.
62: Local Hessian SE and posterior SD on the same parameter scale for all 1,266 active parameters under the same regularized target. Both axes use logarithmic scales; the dashed line denotes equality. Rings identify the six slowest parameters, with posterior-SD/local-SE ratios 1.28–1.52. Coordinate units differ among parameters. MCMC standard errors quantify simulation precision and are separate from the parameter uncertainties shown here.
63: MCMC posterior histograms for the six parameters with the lowest bulk ESS in the original chains. All 5,000 parameter vectors contribute. Bar heights show probability per bin; the panels retain parameter units.
64: Index checks compare observed survey and historical catch-rate indices with simulated observations generated from 1,000 MCMC draws. Each draw supplies a model expectation; random observation errors are then added using the same error assumptions used to fit each index, including the relationships among BTS errors. Lines show median expectations and shading covers the middle 95% of simulated observations at each year. Circles are observed indices and triangles identify existing substitutes. Some simulated values are negative because the fitted Normal error distributions allow them. The BTS overall mismatch measure exceeds its observed value in 0.2% of simulations, indicating that the model rarely reproduces this feature of the BTS data. Biological inputs remain fixed.
69: Recent normalized Model 26.0 fishery selectivity curves and the proposed reference based on averaging the unnormalized curves.
70: Annual Model 26.0 fishery selectivity curves for 2007–2026, each compared with the proposed 2023–2025 raw-curve average rescaled to maximum one. The 2026 curve is estimated without 2026 fishery age compositions.
71: Changes in maximum ABC and OFL under the annual future-selectivity curves relative to the matching Model 26.0 baseline. Rows are ordered by 2027 maximum ABC. These are projection selectivity sensitivities conditional on the same fitted source and projection design.
72: Annual younger-age selectivity measures for 2007–2026 from the Model 26.0. The 2026 estimate is highlighted. Curve-weighted mean age is a shape measure under equal age weights, distinct from a population-weighted selected age.
73: Annual Model 26.0 fishery selectivity and fully selected F35%, a proxy for FMSY, for 2001–2026. Mean selected age uses ages 1–10; SPR uses ages 1–14 and 15+, fixed mortality, maturity and the selected projection spawning weights, and quarter-year spawning timing. Curves are normalized to maximum one. The 2024 figure plotted FMSY.
